definition: The potential, $E^\ominus$ in volts, of a half-cell under standard conditions measured against the standard hydrogen electrode, written for the reduction; the more positive it is, the more easily the oxidized species is reduced.
The reference half-cell, hydrogen gas at $\pu{100 kPa}$ over platinum in $\pu{1.00 mol dm-3}$ $\ce{H^+(aq)}$ at $\pu{298 K}$, whose potential is set at $\pu{0.00 V}$ by convention.

The potential difference of a cell under standard conditions, $E^\ominus_\text{cell} = E^\ominus_\text{cathode} - E^\ominus_\text{anode}$; a positive value means the reaction is spontaneous as written under standard conditions.
The charge carried by one mole of electrons, $F = \pu{9.65e4 C mol-1}$ (data booklet, section 2).
